summary: Recent updates to the Firefox negotiation engine, specifically focusing on the JavaScript Session Establishment Protocol (JSEP) used in WebRTC (the technology behind video calls), have streamlined how the browser manages audio codecs and session parameters. Notably, the system will now **reject the payload type range from 64-95 for RTCP multiplexing**, which enhances compatibility with certain audio configurations, specifically Opus, by accurately parsing its timing options. Additionally, several functions have been improved to use `UniquePtr` for better memory management, ensuring a more efficient and stable handling of codec descriptions and session data. These changes are aimed at reducing errors and improving overall performance during real-time communications in the browser.
